heatmap.title: Dynamic Heatmap
description: This view shows where the selected joints have passed so far. A color appears where a joint has covered that part of the view. Green means fewer passes. Yellow means more passes. Red means the same area has been covered many times. As the video plays, you can watch these colors build up.
compareWithNormal: Compare where the colors build up. Look for red color that stays in the same small area or builds up quickly. More varied movement may spread color across more areas.
technicalDetails: For each selected joint, the app places samples along its path from one frame to the next on a small location grid. Samples from all selected joints are added together, then lightly smoothed so nearby locations form one visible area.

At every frame, the grid contains all samples seen so far. Its colors are scaled using the highest final grid value for that infant: green is lower density, yellow is in the middle, and red is higher density.

lineplot.title: Dynamic Individual Lines
description: Each row shows one selected joint. Choose Speed to see how fast that joint is moving. A higher line means faster movement at that moment. Choose Acceleration to see how fast its speed is changing. Above the middle line means it is speeding up. Below the middle line means it is slowing down.
compareWithNormal: Compare the timing of the lines. Look for several joints speeding up, slowing down, or resting at the same time. More varied movement may have different line shapes and timing across joints.
technicalDetails: Speed is the straight-line distance between a joint's position in two neighboring frames. Signed acceleration is the current speed minus the previous speed, so zero is the middle reference line.
In the dynamic view, each joint is scaled by the largest absolute value seen up to the current frame.

stackedlineplot.title: Dynamic Stacked Lines
description: This view puts the selected joints on one graph. Each color is one joint. Choose Speed to see how fast each joint is moving. Choose Acceleration to see how fast each joint's speed is changing. When Acceleration is selected, the middle line is zero: above it means speeding up and below it means slowing down.
compareWithNormal: Compare the colored lines. Look for several lines rising and falling together with similar shapes and timing. More varied movement may have lines changing at different times.
technicalDetails: Speed and signed acceleration use the same calculations as the individual-line view. All selected joints share one scale, based on the largest absolute value seen up to the current frame.
This shared scale makes the heights of different colored lines directly comparable within the graph.

episodes.title: Dynamic Movement Episodes
description: This view shows only times when a selected joint has a big speed or acceleration change. Acceleration means how fast speed is changing. Each bar is one time period. A wider bar lasts longer. A taller bar is stronger. With Acceleration selected, bars above the middle line show speeding up and bars below it show slowing down. Bars can change as the video plays because the app is still learning what counts as a big change.
compareWithNormal: Compare when the bars begin and end. Look for bars from several joints that start and end together and have similar widths or heights. More varied movement may have bars spread out across joints and time.
technicalDetails: The app calculates speed or signed acceleration at each frame. It finds periods whose absolute value is above a threshold based on the current peak and average value. Positive and negative acceleration periods are kept separate.

Bar width represents the number of frames in the period. Bar height represents its peak magnitude. The threshold is recalculated as new frames arrive, so dynamic bars can appear, disappear, join, or split.

componentvariance.title: Dynamic Movement Patterns
description: Each box shows one repeated movement pattern found in this recording. Click a box to see that pattern on the body view. The bars show which body areas are most involved. Longer bars and larger percentages mean that area is more involved. A red bold percentage with an exclamation mark means one area is above 40%.
compareWithNormal: Compare which body areas are most involved in each pattern. Look for patterns that keep focusing on the same joints or the same side of the body.
technicalDetails: The component analysis separates the recording into repeated motion patterns. For each pattern, the displayed percentage is that joint group's share of the component variance; all displayed shares add to 100%.
In the dynamic view, values are recomputed with frames available up to the current frame. The alert appears when an individual displayed contribution is greater than 40%.

heatmap.title: Static Heatmap
description: Each row is one selected joint. The color shows how far that joint has moved in total up to each point in the video. Green means less total distance. Yellow means more. Red means the joint has moved the farthest. The vertical line marks the frame shown in the body view.
compareWithNormal: Compare how the row colors build up over time. Look for several rows changing at the same time and at a similar rate. More varied movement may have rows changing at different times.
technicalDetails: For each joint, the app adds the straight-line distance moved between every pair of neighboring frames. Each cell shows that running total at a particular frame.
All selected rows are scaled by the largest running total in that infant's selected data. Green is lower total distance, yellow is in the middle, and red is higher total distance.
